headline: BRICS Adopts New Delhi Declaration as Marcos Joins Summit as ASEAN Chair
seoTitle: BRICS Adopts New Delhi Declaration as Marcos Attends Summit | FMB News
seoDescription: BRICS leaders adopted the New Delhi Declaration on Middle East tensions, trade and global governance as President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. attended the summit as ASEAN chair.
deck: The consensus declaration urges restraint in the Middle East, criticizes unilateral trade measures and calls for reforms in global governance. The Philippines is not a BRICS member; President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. is attending the New Delhi summit as ASEAN chair.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: BRICS leaders adopted the New Delhi Declaration on September 12 during the first day of their summit in India, reaching consensus on a document covering geopolitical conflicts, trade, global governance, energy and development priorities.

Reuters reported that the declaration expressed deep concern over escalating Middle East tensions, urged maximum restraint and reaffirmed support for resolving international disputes through dialogue, consultation and diplomacy. The declaration also raised concerns about unilateral tariff and non-tariff measures that BRICS members say distort trade and create uncertainty for developing economies.

A text of the declaration published through the office of India's prime minister also calls for more representative global governance and reforms to international financial institutions to better reflect the growing role of emerging markets and developing economies.

sections.heading: Philippine context
paragraphs: President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. is in New Delhi for the September 12-13 summit after accepting an invitation from Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Philippine reporting says Marcos is participating in his capacity as chair of ASEAN.

The Philippines is not a BRICS member, so the New Delhi Declaration is not a Philippine treaty commitment. Marcos's participation instead places the Philippines and ASEAN in discussions involving major emerging economies at a time of heightened pressure on energy markets, shipping routes and the international trading system.

sections.heading: Why this matters to Filipinos
paragraphs: The summit's focus on Middle East instability has direct economic relevance to the Philippines because the country depends heavily on imported petroleum and is exposed to changes in global shipping, insurance and energy costs. FMB News has separately reported on disruptions affecting major Middle East energy and maritime routes.

The declaration's positions on trade and reform of global institutions also matter because the Philippines is an export- and investment-dependent economy that operates within rules set by institutions such as the World Trade Organization, World Bank and International Monetary Fund.

Marcos's presence gives the Philippines an opportunity to represent ASEAN perspectives in a forum that includes several of the world's largest emerging economies, but any concrete Philippine benefit will depend on actual agreements, investments or diplomatic outcomes rather than summit participation alone.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: The summit continues on September 13. The most important Philippine developments to watch are any formal bilateral agreements, investment commitments, energy or trade arrangements, or ASEAN-related initiatives announced during Marcos's meetings in New Delhi.

FMB News will also watch whether the summit produces additional language or concrete mechanisms on Middle East de-escalation, energy security, local-currency trade, institutional reform or supply-chain resilience beyond the declaration itself.

audit.socialCaption: BRICS leaders have adopted the New Delhi Declaration, calling for restraint in the Middle East while raising concerns over unilateral trade measures and pushing reforms in global governance. President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. is attending the New Delhi summit as ASEAN chair. The Philippines is not a BRICS member, so the declaration is not a Philippine treaty commitment.
verificationNotes: The declaration's adoption is verified by Reuters and by the declaration text published through the office of India's prime minister.
The article distinguishes the Philippines' status from BRICS membership: President Marcos is attending as ASEAN chair, not as the leader of a BRICS member state.
Philstar.com and Inquirer.net independently corroborate Marcos's New Delhi trip and summit participation.
The article does not treat broad declaration language as a binding Philippine commitment or as proof of concrete investment outcomes.

Philippine relevance is tied to energy exposure, trade, shipping and ASEAN diplomacy, while the article explicitly notes that concrete benefits depend on actual subsequent agreements or implementation.
